title: Role-mapping hire cascade and initial 90d sprint plan
content:
Purpose: capture a repeatable, light-weight hire cascade and 30/60/90 activation sprint for cross-functional IC hires (product, infra, SRE, solutions). This doc bundles: a pragmatic headcount/hire ordering plan, interviewer rubric tuned to production-first engineering at Redwood, and a practical onboarding checklist emphasizing early impact and peer pairing.

Summary/high-level approach:
- Goal: get new ICs productive on a measurable component within 60 days, and able to independently own a small customer-facing change by 90 days.
- Philosophy: bias to ship, reduce ramp friction with clear early milestones, pair across teams to transfer tribal knowledge quickly.
- Audience: recruiters, hiring managers, interviewers, hiring committee, people-ops onboarding squad.

1) Hire cascade and role-mapping (ordering + rationale)
- Phase A (Q1 hires): 2 infra engineers (runtime), 1 product-engineer (console), 1 SRE focused on observability backlog. Rationale: infra + observability reduces query latency incidents and improves deploy confidence for upcoming Dedicated launch.
- Phase B (Q2 hires): 2 solutions engineers, 1 QA/automation. Rationale: scale customer enablement and reduce manual validation work.
- Notes to recruiter: open reqs should include explicit cross-team pairing expectations in JD; list typical first-30 and first-90 deliverables.

2) Interview rubric (single-page, used by all interviewers)
- Overall: score 1-5 (1=insufficient, 5=exceptional). Hiring threshold baseline: average >= 3.5 and no critical 1s.
- Competency buckets (weighting in parentheses):
  - Core technical (40%): system design / runtime/infra fundamentals; depth for role.
  - Problem solving & debugging (20%): triage historical production issue, root cause thinking.
  - Product judgement & scope (15%): shipping tradeoffs, prioritization for user impact.
  - Collaboration & communication (15%): cross-team communication, async docs, code reviews.
  - Culture / mission fit (10%): reliability-first, cost-conscious, iterative.

- Rubric anchors (examples):
  - Core technical: 5 = designed a scalable inference pipeline, quantified SLOs/latency tradeoffs; 3 = good architecture choices but missing operational knobs; 1 = architecture missing major failure modes.
  - Debugging: 5 = walks through live incident postmortem and provides remediation + prevention plan; 3 = reasonable triage steps but misses follow-on testing; 1 = cannot propose root-cause hypotheses.
  - Collab: 5 = clear examples of cross-functional leadership, shipped with PM/infra; 3 = good collaborator in small teams; 1 = poor communication evidence.

- Interview flow suggestions (30–60 min slots):
  - Core tech (system/architecture) 30–45 min
  - Debugging / retrospective 20–30 min
  - Behavioral / collaboration 15–20 min

- Calibration notes for interviewers: always comment on candidate’s tradeoff framing (cost/latency/complexity). Use the shared scorecard (link above) and add explicit pass/fail flags for security/compliance concerns.

3) Candidate experience and recruiter playbook
- Pre-screen (30 min): recruiter + hiring manager alignment call; send a 2-page hiring packet with role expectations and sample first-30/first-90 deliverables.
- Loop composition: 1 hiring manager, 2 peers (team), 1 cross-team infra reviewer, 1 skip-level (for senior ICs). Keep loop to <= 4 interviews in first pass.
- Offer timeline target: 5 business days from final loop to offer. Hard stop: must escalate if beyond 10 business days.

4) Onboarding checklist (Day 0 -> 90) — actionable, assign owners and acceptance criteria
- Day -1 (pre-start): equipment ordered, accounts provisioned, manager sends 30/60/90 with first sprint goal. Owner: People-ops / IT.
- Day 0–7: orientation block, security briefing, runbook reading (top 5 runbooks), pair with assigned buddy for environment setup. Acceptance criteria: can run local dev stack + run basic inference end-to-end. Owner: manager + buddy.
- Week 2–4 (first sprint): small bugfix or doc improvement scoped to produce a merged PR and deployment to staging. Acceptance criteria: merged PR, test coverage added or updated. Owner: manager + mentor.
- Day 30 review: 1:1 structured review — manager, mentor, and peer brief. Evidence: merged PR, shadowed an on-call rotation, written 1-page summary of stack.
- Day 45–60 (second sprint): owner of a small feature or optimizations (e.g., a quantization profile evaluation, batching config tweak, or console UX polish). Acceptance criteria: feature in staging with measurable metric change (latency/CPU/cost) or merged UX improvements. Owner: PM + engineering lead.
- Day 60 review: present a 10-min demo and a short retro on ramp blockers. Manager to write a 1-paragraph plan for continued growth.
- Day 90 (graduation): independent ownership of a small cross-team task and a follow-up success metric. Manager signs off for full production access.

5) Early evaluation and success metrics (what to measure)
- Activity: PRs merged, docs created/edited, issues triaged (counts + quality).
- Impact: measurable change in a metric tied to the sprint (latency p50/p95, cost per token, time-to-restore).
- Qualitative: peer feedback on collaboration and communication.
- Recommendation checkpoints: 30-day light-pass, 60-day go/no-go on independent ownership, 90-day graduation.

6) Mentorship & pairing plan (to accelerate knowledge transfer)
- 2-week pairing schedule for first 30 days: buddy (developer), infra mentor, and product pairing session. Each week includes at least 4 hours of live pairing.
- Shadow on-call: first two rotations as observer, weeks 3–6 take escalating responsibilities with mentor oversight.

7) Interviewer checklist + calibration anchors (practical tips)
- Provide explicit time markers in the interview for candidate to ask clarifying q’s.
- Ask candidate to explain tradeoffs wrt cost and reliability — mark score if they bring unit economics into decisions.
- For senior roles, include a short architecture whiteboard where candidate explicitly lists failure modes and mitigation.

8) Open questions / decisions to finalize
- Should we require a small take-home for infra roles? Pros: targeted signal on implementation. Cons: adds friction and long lead time. (Action: people-ops + eng hiring to decide by 2025-02-28 — owner: Diego Morales).
- How strict should quantification be for 60-day deliverable? Some roles (research-adjacent) may not have immediate metric impact. Proposal: allow alternative deliverables (e.g., architecture doc + spike) with manager pre-approval.

9) Links & calibration artifacts
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.company/people/role-mapping-v2
- Hiring tracker board: https://jira.redwood.company/secure/RapidBoard.jspa?rapidView=32
- Sample scorecard template: Slack pinned in #people-ops-onboarding

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a short "first-week checklist" PDF for candidates (helps expectation setting).
- Add a checklist for private deployment readiness for hires who will touch customer infra (security attestations, background checks).
- Track ramp signals in a lightweight spreadsheet (columns: name, start-date, 30d-evidence, 60d-evidence, 90d-signoff).

Unresolved: capture which cross-team projects are priority to seed knowledge sharing — I'll follow up with product and infra leads next week.

-- end of draft: feedback welcome from hiring managers and eng leads.
